surfaces.rationale: Acorn's executable definitions: machine encodings, arithmetic, the learners, feature lifecycle, world, host runner, checkpoint and viewer protocol, and the native drivers that consume them. Its binary32 and binary64 operations use Lean's core float model, which depends on Classical.choice, so choice-free is not attainable. Checked execution holds because the library declares no extern, replacement, unsafe or partial code and its executing modules import only the Lean toolchain, so every boundary its definitions and eight executables reach belongs to the toolchain's own trusted base. One further module, Acorn.Decisions, registers the library's decision functions with their Regula contracts: it imports Regula's contract type and decision attribute, and no executable or other module imports it, so no entry point links the closed values and the argument structures that it declares. Native arithmetic, the Lean runtime and the POSIX effects reached through toolchain primitives stay trusted, and the spawned checkpoint-sync process is outside the account.

Contracts about the executing Acorn definitions, with the supporting Mathlib mathematics stated under explicit hypotheses. AcornVerif.Decisions states the Regula decision contracts whose proofs need this library. Mathlib's real analysis and classical reasoning use Classical.choice. One bridge module connects the executing binary32 and binary64 wrappers to FloatLib's real-valued rounding theorems, which depend on the same three axioms; no other module imports FloatLib. The library has no executable. Execution stays report because checked was measured to fail with Regula v0.3.0: RG3002 (https://rbeauchamp.github.io/regula/v/0.3.0/rules/RG3002/) fired 296 times, every finding in AcornVerif, naming compiled definitions there that reach Bool.rec, List.rec or Option.rec. Each is reached as a compiler-simplification boundary and as the partial-computation implementation that Mathlib.Util.CompileInductive generates, and Mathlib owns both.

Native entry points, embedded provenance and viewer resources over the Acorn definitions. They depend on Classical.choice through those definitions and core string operations, so choice-free is not attainable. Checked execution holds because the library declares no extern, replacement, unsafe or partial code and imports only Acorn and the Lean toolchain, so the runtime, process, filesystem and socket primitives its definitions and three executables reach belong to the toolchain's own trusted base. Those primitives stay trusted, and the reviewed C fsync helper runs as a spawned process outside the account.

The offline Lake launcher that admits provisioned dependencies for every gate, including this audit. It imports only the pinned toolchain and maps locked dependencies to provisioned paths before Lake loads the workspace. The core string and JSON operations it uses depend on Classical.choice, so choice-free is not attainable. Checked execution holds because the module declares no extern, replacement, unsafe or partial code, so every boundary its definitions reach belongs to the toolchain's own trusted base. The launcher runs interpreted with no Lake executable, and the Lake process it spawns is outside the account.

excluded-libraries.rationale: Reviewed build and verification tooling, an explicit trust boundary under AGENTS.md and outside the application's proof claim. It loads compiled environments with unsafe Lean APIs and runs the gates that admit the claimed surfaces; every tool module is admitted individually by AcornModuleInventory.toolingModules.
